clinician.trajectory_summary: A 28-year-old male presented with a 2-month history of nonproductive progressive cough and left flank pain. Physical examination revealed abdominal distention with a large mass in the left upper quadrant and left flank tenderness, with stable vital signs. MRI of the abdomen with contrast demonstrated a 155 × 140 × 150 mm mass in the left suprarenal fossa with fine lobulated margin, central cystic changes, diffusion restriction, and heterogeneous enhancement pattern. Metastatic disease was identified including a lymph node at the left side of the abdominal aorta and multiple metastatic nodules in the lower lobes of both lungs and liver. Tissue biopsy was performed, and microscopic examination showed small round cells on hematoxylin and eosin staining. Immunohistochemistry demonstrated positive staining for FLI-1, Synaptophysin, and CK, with negative staining for LCA, WT-1, DESMIN, Myogenin, phox-B2, CD99, SOX10, Chromogranin, and GATA3. The pathology report was compatible with renal PNET/Ewing sarcoma. The pulmonary metastases identified on imaging correlate with the patient's presenting symptom of nonproductive cough.
